messages:
hani: hey all, totally new here — trying to get kubectl working for my team namespace `infra-utils`. I pasted the kubeconfig from the onboarding page but `kubectl config current-context` shows `redwood-dev@redwood-cluster` and `kubectl get pods -n infra-utils` errors with `Forbidden`:
```
Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User "system:anonymous" cannot list resource "pods" in API group "" in the namespace "infra-utils"
```
Not sure why it's anonymous. I set up Okta SSO earlier today. Anyone seen this?

renee: welcome @hani! that anonymous error usually means the kubeconfig isn't using the exec auth plugin (okta) or the token isn't being picked up. run `kubectl config view --raw` and check the user section for an `exec` block or `token:` field. should look like `exec: { apiVersion: client.authentication.k8s.io/v1beta1, command: okta-aws-creds ... }` (we use okta-oidc plugin name `redwood-oidc` here).

hani: `kubectl config view --raw` shows a user block with `auth-provider` not `exec`, and no token. maybe I accidentally downloaded the old static kubeconfig blob.

infra-bot: Access request #AK-14200 created for user hani. Approver: @renee. Status: pending. Link: https://redwood.internal/tickets/AK-14200

platform-oncall: quick debug tip: if your kubeconfig was generated via the web UI you might have two files merged. do `grep -n "name: redwood-dev" ~/.kube/config` to see duplicates. we recommend `kubectl config view --flatten --merge=false > ~/.kube/config.clean` and then `mv ~/.kube/config.clean ~/.kube/config`. after that run `kubectl config set-credentials hani --exec-command=redwood-oidc --exec-arg=get-token` if your client supports it, or re-download the kubeconfig from the onboarding portal selecting "OIDC (Okta)" option.

hani: tried flattening, but still getting anonymous. maybe my local kubeconfig was created by `eksctl` before and has a different user block name. how do i inspect which user kubectl is using for that context?

renee: run `kubectl config view -o jsonpath='{.contexts[?(@.name=="redwood-dev@redwood-cluster")].context.user}'` to print the user name. then `kubectl config view -o jsonpath='{.users[?(@.name=="PUT_USER_HERE")].user}'` to show the user config. replace PUT_USER_HERE with what you got.

hani: got `redwood-hani` as the user but the `user` block is empty except `username: hani` (no token/exec). weird.

taylor: I can push you the correct OIDC kubeconfig snippet. If you want immediate access, @renee can approve `sandbox` role which we temporarily bind to `infra-utils` for onboarding. Otherwise I'll attach the proper exec-plugin config to your ticket. Also note: once you have access, create a context with a user that maps to your GitHub/AD identity to keep things clean.

renee: approved AK-14200 for 72h trial. @platform-oncall please bind `edit` to `onboard-hani` for namespace `infra-utils` until EOD +3.

infra-bot: Access request AK-14200 updated: approved by renee. Temporary binding `onboard-hani` -> `infra-utils` created. Expires in 72h.

hani: thanks team! after the bind I re-downloaded the kubeconfig (OIDC option) and now `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n infra-utils` returns `yes` and `kubectl get pods -n infra-utils` works. also made a `context` named `hani-infra-utils` with namespace baked in. feel much better. :relieved:
